title: Canonical positivity and tricanonical embedding of a nodal curve
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $C$ a proper connected reduced scheme over $\Omega$, pure of dimension one, with at worst nodal singularities [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. Write $g=\dim_\Omega H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ and assume $g\geq2$ [def-sc-sheaf-cohomology-functor]. Let $\omega_C$ be its dualizing line: the invertible module representing $F\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_\Omega(H^1(C,F),\Omega)$ on quasi-coherent modules $F$. For every irreducible component $Z$ of $C$, let $\nu_Z:\widetilde Z\to C$ be its reduced component normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], put $g_Z=\dim_\Omega H^1(\widetilde Z,\mathcal O_{\widetilde Z})$, and let $b_Z$ be the number of points over the nonsmooth locus of $C$. Then $\omega_C$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] if and only if every component with $g_Z=0$ has $b_Z\geq3$ and every component with $g_Z=1$ has $b_Z\geq1$. Whenever these equivalent conditions hold, $H^1(C,\omega_C^{\otimes3})=0$ and the complete linear system gives a closed immersion
$$C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_\Omega(H^0(C,\omega_C^{\otimes3})).$$
The projective bundle uses one-dimensional quotients, as in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], and its tautological line pulls back to $\omega_C^{\otimes3}$.

proof.text:
The structure map $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is separated and of finite type by the definition of properness. On every affine chart the coordinate algebra is of finite presentation: a field is Noetherian, and the finite-type-over-Noetherian algebra theorem applies. Thus $f$ is locally of finite presentation; its quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness follow from finite type and separatedness, so $f$ is finitely presented. It is flat because every module over the field $\Omega$ is a vector space and hence flat. The current nodal theorem asks explicitly that nonsmooth closed geometric points have completed local algebra $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ and the other points be smooth; these are exactly the assumed at-worst-nodal singularities over $\Omega$. Apply the relative-dualizing theorem for proper flat nodal curves: its line on this fibre is the fibre's Serre-duality module. This line and the given $\omega_C$ represent the same functor and hence are isomorphic: the maps corresponding to the identity elements under the representing bijections are inverse by naturality. The proper-nodal dualizing base-change theorem supplies, on every normalized component, a proper smooth connected curve and
$$d_Z:=\deg(\nu_Z^*\omega_C)=2g_Z-2+b_Z.$$
Thus $\omega_C$ is the canonical nodal adjunction line $\omega_{C/\Omega}$ of that theorem, with its Jacobian-normalized datum. It explicitly counts both branches of a self-node. Its hypotheses require neither projectivity nor a smooth generic fibre, and are all satisfied here.

proof.text: Apply the current normalized-component ampleness criterion to $X=C$ and $\mathcal M=\omega_C$: properness is assumed, the dimension is one, and $C_{\mathrm{red}}=C$ because $C$ is reduced. Its one-dimensional reduced components and their normalizations are precisely the $Z$ and $\nu_Z$ of Step 1. The criterion requires neither projectivity nor smoothness of $C$. It says precisely that $\omega_C$ is ample if and only if every $d_Z>0$. Substituting Step 1, for $g_Z=0$ the inequality is $-2+b_Z>0$, or $b_Z\ge3$; for $g_Z=1$ it is $b_Z>0$, or $b_Z\ge1$; for $g_Z\ge2$ it is automatic since $2g_Z-2\ge2$ and $b_Z\ge0$. This proves both directions of the stated equivalence.

proof.text: Assume these conditions. Apply the existing stable pointed linear-series theorem to $k=\Omega$ and $C$, with no markings ($r=0$, $D=0$), so that $M=\omega_{C/\Omega}$, which is $\omega_C$ by Step 1. Its hypotheses are those of the statement: $C$ is proper, nonempty, connected, reduced, nodal and pure of dimension one over the algebraically closed $\Omega$, and its normalized reduced components are the $\nu_Z$ of Step 1. With $m_V=0$ its positivity hypothesis $2g(V)-2+b_V>0$ is $d_Z>0$ for every $Z$, which Step 2 showed is equivalent to the stated conditions: for $g_Z=0$ it means $b_Z\ge3$, for $g_Z=1$ it means $b_Z\ge1$, and for $g_Z\ge2$ it always holds. Take $m=3$. The theorem gives $H^i(C,\omega_C^{\otimes3})=0$ for all $i>0$, in particular $H^1(C,\omega_C^{\otimes3})=0$. It also says that $L=\omega_C^{\otimes3}$ is globally generated, so the evaluation map $H^0(C,L)\otimes_\Omega\mathcal O_C\to L$ is surjective. Finally, its complete linear system gives a closed immersion into the projective space of one-dimensional quotients of $H^0(C,L)$. By the projective-bundle quotient theorem with $S=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $\mathcal E=H^0(C,L)$, this is the morphism attached to the evaluation quotient, and it carries a quotient-compatible isomorphism $a^*\mathcal O_P(1)\cong L$. Hence the tautological line pulls back to $\omega_C^{\otimes3}$.
